title: Book IX
frozenSupport: Book IX opens by calling injustice and lying impiety because rational beings are made for one another and universal nature is aligned with truth.
Marcus compresses Stoic sufficiency into present opinion, present conduct directed to social good, and present contentment with what happens.
The chapter emphasizes one intelligent soul among rational beings and a natural pull toward union, co-operation, and common interest.
It repeatedly orders the ruling faculty to wipe out imagination, cast out trouble, and recognize that disturbance comes from opinion rather than externals.
Later sections develop an extended anti-anger discipline built on self-examination, compulsion-awareness, mortality, and mildness as true strength.
allowedClaims: wrongdoing violates shared rational nature before it merely offends private preference
truthfulness is part of living in alignment with universal nature
present social conduct matters more than grievance loops
anger usually adds more pain than the original offense
mildness and correction can be stronger than rage
doNotClaim: that injustice does not matter because everything is opinion
that Marcus treats lying as harmless if intentions are good
that anti-anger discipline forbids correction or accountability
that shared rational nature means all people already act wisely
